definitions.explanation: Describes something or someone that is well-ordered, properly arranged, or meeting expected standards. Used for appearance, behavior, work, and arrangements. The base adverb きちんと means 'properly' or 'neatly.'

examples.japanese: きちんとした{服装|ふくそう}で{来|き}てください。
きちんとした{挨拶|あいさつ}ができる{人|ひと}は{好|こう}{印象|いんしょう}を{与|あた}える。
examples.english: A person who can greet properly makes a good impression.

examples.japanese: きちんとした{生活|せいかつ}を{送|おく}るために、{毎朝|まいあさ}{同|おな}じ{時間|じかん}に{起|お}きるようにしている。
examples.english: In order to lead a well-ordered life, I try to wake up at the same time every morning.

notes:
USAGE:
きちんとした is the prenominal (modifying) form of きちんとする. The base adverb きちんと is extremely common and can modify verbs directly (きちんと{並|なら}べる 'line up neatly').

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- きちんとした{服装|ふくそう} (proper attire)
- きちんとした{生活|せいかつ} (well-ordered lifestyle)
- きちんとした{対応|たいおう} (proper handling/response)
- きちんとした{説明|せつめい} (a proper explanation)
- きちんと{片付|かたづ}ける (tidy up properly)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ちゃんとした: proper/decent — very similar but slightly more colloquial
- しっかりした: solid/reliable — emphasizes dependability rather than neatness
- {整|ととの}った: well-arranged — focuses on physical order and preparation
